beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: If you have ever been told that you were born guilty — that a baby arrives in this world already condemned for something a man did in a garden — this one is for you.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Adam and Eve took the fruit, and everything changed. The gate closed behind them. Death entered the world. And heaven watched it happen — without panic.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Because the Fall was not the plan breaking. It was the plan beginning.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Outside Eden the ground fought them. Thorns. Sweat. Loss. And also — for the first time — children. Morning laughter. Work worth doing. Choices that actually meant something.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Blessed be the name of God: for because of my transgression my eyes are opened, and in this life I shall have joy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is Adam — the man the whole mess gets blamed on — praising God for what the Fall opened up. And Eve saw it first, and saw it whole:

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: Were it not for our transgression we never should have had seed, and never should have known good and evil, and the joy of our redemption.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Seed. Knowledge. Redemption. No children without the Fall. No growth without a real dark to choose against. And no need for a Savior — no Savior given.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So what about the guilt? Who pays for Eden? Here is what God actually says about that.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: We believe that men will be punished for their own sins, and not for Adam's transgression.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Not for Adam's transgression. You will answer for what you choose. You will never answer for what Adam chose. There is no inherited guilt. There is no baby born condemned.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Little children are whole, for they are not capable of committing sin; wherefore the curse of Adam is taken from them in me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The curse of Adam is taken from them in me. Every baby ever born arrives clean — already covered, already paid for, before their first breath.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The devil has spent centuries teaching the world to fear God over Eden — a God who condemns infants, a guilt you carry for another man's choice. Now you know. That was never your Father.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Fall brought death — and Christ answers death, for everyone, free. The Fall brought sin — and you answer only for yours, with a Redeemer standing by. Adam fell that men might be. And men are, that they might have joy.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: You were not born guilty. You were born wanted — into a plan built to bring you joy.
